set.approach: On the Icefields Parkway, drive to the Weeping Wall and look for a cluster of big boulders some distance south of it; pull off onto the highway shoulder. Go to the cave entrance behind the Stratus Boulder; the route is on the left and climbs out of the cave mouth.
set.descent_text: Walk down the boulder by fourth-class ground from the anchor; look it over before you climb.

set.approach: Drive up the Maligne Lake Road to the first Medicine Lake viewpoint and park. Follow the far shore of the lake, away from the road, to Watchtower Creek, then head up the creek and pick up the trail. Follow the main trail up the creek; the Upper Tier is the large wall on your left, cut by a ledge. To get up onto the ledge, go right past the end of the wall and fork left shortly before the plank bridge, then double back along the cliff band on a good trail. Hot Carl is the most obvious flake system and left-facing corner, running to the top of the wall; it is the second bolt line from the right, past the hole in the wall where water pours out.

review.notes: Area pages for the approach; route page for position.

set.approach: Park in the round, sandy pullout on the Icefields Parkway south of the Kerkeslin Campground entrance. Behind it a small open field is hidden by trees; go through the opening toward Kerkeslin and take the narrow trail slightly to the right through a poplar forest. After the steeper section begins, a fork leads left (if you can already see short cliffs ahead you have gone too far); follow that trail up through a narrow canyon with a creek. Keep going until the Main Wall, with many bolted routes, is on your left; the Warm Up Wall sits on the far side of the drainage from it. Biting the Dust is the obvious groove in the middle, between the other two bolt lines on the wall.

review.notes: Youth Lagoon and wall pages for the approach; route page for position.

set.approach: Take Highway 93A south from Jasper, past Athabasca Falls, to Leech Lake and park at the pullout or at the small one a little further on the left. set.approach: Drive the Snaring road past the campsites to where it becomes a dirt road, continuing to the big U-turn on a cliffy stretch above Jasper Lake. Once you are heading downhill you will spot the crag to the left; leave the car on the right beside the open field, clear of the road. The crag sits above the larger, lower cliff band. Walk up beside the powerlines to the second pole, continue a bit, then bear right on scrambly ground to top out the lower cliff band, then walk toward the obvious slabs uphill. The route begins where the rock steepens, to the right of a big slab crack that becomes a chimney.
set.descent_text: Lowering off drags the rope across the long slab above the second roof. Rappelling is awkward as well, because the fall line is far from the bolt line.

review.notes: Route page for start and descent; area page for approach.
